categories.name: Options

options.summary: Set the boot image’s flash I/O mode.
options.detail: Select qio, qout, dio or dout to match the flash wiring and chip. The default keep preserves the bootable image header unless ESPTOOL_FM supplies an override. The v5 parser also recognizes the deprecated --flash_mode spelling. Spellings: --flash-mode and -fm.

esptool 5.0.2: use exact chip-specific tokens, not an arbitrary number. MB tokens denote MiB (1048576 bytes); ESP8266 KB tokens denote KiB. ESP8266 also has -c1 layout tokens; ESP32-S2/S3/P4 permit additional larger sizes. keep preserves the image header; detect reads flash ID and the documented detection-failure fallback is 4MB. The default is keep unless ESPTOOL_FS overrides it. These fields apply to a bootable-image header at the chip's bootloader offset; supported sizes depend on chip, ROM/stub and flash hardware. Other releases require verification. For example, 4MB means 4 MiB. The v5 parser also recognizes the deprecated --flash_size spelling. Spellings: --flash-size and -fs.
options.summary: Set header flash size (4MB means 4 MiB).

options.detail: esptool 5.0.2: lowercase m in these literal tokens denotes MHz, not minutes or millihertz. ESP32 uses 20m/26m/40m/80m; ESP32-C2 uses 15m/20m/30m/60m; ESP32-H2 uses 12m/16m/24m/48m; other target-specific sets are documented in the flash parameter reference. keep preserves the image header; the default is keep unless ESPTOOL_FF overrides it. Hardware must support the selected clock, and the option only changes applicable bootable-image headers. Other chips/releases require their own verified table. For example, 40m means 40 MHz where the chip accepts it. The v5 parser also recognizes the deprecated --flash_freq spelling. The 5.6.0 parser lists 32m and 64m, but none of its 15 built-in chip types can encode either clock in a boot image header. Spellings: --flash-freq and -ff.
options.summary: Set the boot SPI clock (40m means 40 MHz).
Erase the entire flash before writing.
options.detail: Normally only sectors touched by a supplied image are erased. A partial sector is erased as a whole. This flag also erases regions outside every supplied image. Spellings: --erase-all and -e.

options.summary: Encrypt all supplied images during writing.
options.detail: Requires a chip configured for encrypted downloads and suitably aligned byte offsets. Use --encrypt-files to encrypt selected pairs instead. The two forms cannot be combined.

options.summary: Override flash protection and image compatibility checks.
options.detail: This permits writes normally blocked for secure boot, flash encryption or incompatible image headers. A wrong bootloader or plaintext write can leave the device unable to boot.

options.summary: Compress the serial transfer.
options.detail: Compression affects bytes sent to the device. It does not shrink the stored image. Enabled by default with the flasher stub. Excludes --no-compress. Spellings: -z and --compress.

options.summary: Send the image without transfer compression.
options.detail: Uncompressed transfer is the default with the global --no-stub option. Affects serial traffic only. Excludes --compress. Spellings: -u and --no-compress.

options.detail: Place the help flag after the command to list its flash options. Before the command it shows global help. Spellings: --help and -h.

options.summary: Select the SPI flash connection.
options.detail: For a custom pin mapping, pass five GPIO numbers in CLK,Q,D,HD,CS order as one comma-separated argument. SPI and HSPI select predefined connections. In 5.6.0 the built-in custom pin mapping is supported on ESP32, ESP32-S2, ESP32-S3 and ESP32-C3. Spellings: --spi-connection and -sc.

options.summary: Hide transfer progress.
options.detail: After the command -p suppresses the progress display. Before the command -p PORT selects the serial port. Spellings: --no-progress and -p.

options.summary: Encrypt only the listed flash images.
options.detail: Supply complete byte-offset and filename pairs after this option. Put ordinary address/file pairs first so the option cannot consume them. Quote filenames with spaces. Do not combine with --encrypt.

options.summary: Continue despite failed encryption prechecks.
options.detail: An encrypted write can proceed despite an unexpected encryption configuration or key check. This flag cannot program a missing key or enable disabled encrypted downloads. Compatibility spelling in 5.6.0: --ignore_flash_encryption_efuse_setting.

options.summary: Reflash sectors that differ from earlier images.
options.detail: Available from 5.2.0. Put previous filenames after the new address/file pairs in matching order. The literal skip leaves that position out. In 5.6.0 a mismatch after a partial write triggers a full rewrite. Encrypted writes and --erase-all fall back to full writes.

options.summary: Skip verification of unchanged images during fast reflashing.
options.detail: From 5.3.0 this requires --diff-with and excludes --skip-flashed. Use it only if flash still holds the baseline. Written files are verified and a failed partial write is retried in full.

options.summary: Trust the supplied baseline during fast reflashing.
options.detail: 5.2.0 uses this spelling to suppress MD5 checks with --diff-with. In 5.3.0 through 5.6.0 it is the deprecated spelling of --trust-flash-content. Those releases still verify written files.

options.summary: Skip images whose MD5 digest already matches flash.
options.detail: Introduced in 5.2.0, which also checks files paired by --diff-with. In 5.3.0 through 5.6.0 this independent check excludes --diff-with and --trust-flash-content. Before the command -s is the global silent flag. Spellings: --skip-flashed and -s.

description: Options for esptool write-flash. esptool v5 or newer, hyphenated CLI; no automatic rewrite to legacy spellings. ADDRESS is a byte offset (decimal or base-prefixed, such as 0x1000); FILE is its filename. Enter complete ADDRESS FILE pairs. Numerical tables are verified only for 5.0.2.
